name: Python
cons: Slower than compiled languages
GIL limits threading
Not great for mobile
futureScope: Dominant in AI, data, scientific computing. Will remain #1 for the next decade.

name: JavaScript
cons: Weak typing
Callback complexity
futureScope: Ubiquitous for web; TypeScript adoption growing rapidly.

name: Java
cons: Verbose
Slow startup
Memory heavy
futureScope: Backbone of enterprise & Android; Spring Boot demand very high in India.

name: Go
cons: Less mature libraries in some domains
No generics until recently
futureScope: Rising fast for cloud-native & backend microservices.

name: Rust
cons: Steep learning curve
Longer compile times
futureScope: Replacing C++ in critical systems. Loved by developers 8 years running.

name: C
pros: Small language with direct systems concepts
Useful for embedded and operating-system fundamentals
cons: Manual memory management
Limited built-in abstractions
Undefined behaviour can be difficult to debug
futureScope: A foundational systems language that remains useful in embedded, firmware, operating-system, and performance-critical work.

name: C++
cons: Complex language and build tooling
Manual memory and lifetime concepts require care
futureScope: Important for game engines, embedded software, high-performance services, and existing large systems.

name: TypeScript
cons: Requires a build or runtime toolchain in many projects
Types do not validate untrusted runtime data by themselves
futureScope: A widely used choice for maintainable frontend and Node.js applications; learn JavaScript fundamentals first.

name: SQL
cons: Database dialects differ
Poorly designed queries can be expensive
Not a general-purpose application language
futureScope: Essential for software, analytics, data engineering, and database work across industries.

name: C#
pros: Good support for web, cloud, and games
cons: Some roles are concentrated in particular ecosystems
Framework knowledge is needed beyond syntax
futureScope: Useful for enterprise development on .NET, Azure services, and Unity-based games.

name: Kotlin
cons: Smaller ecosystem than Java in some areas
Multiplatform libraries and tooling vary by use case
futureScope: A strong option for Android applications and a growing choice for JVM and multiplatform development.

name: Swift
cons: Apple tooling is most accessible on Apple hardware
Fewer opportunities outside Apple-platform work
futureScope: Relevant for iOS and Apple-platform development; demand depends on mobile product teams.

name: PHP
cons: Legacy code quality varies
Framework and version practices need attention
futureScope: Continues to support a large portion of web infrastructure and modern application development with current PHP frameworks.

name: R
cons: Less common for general application development
Package and deployment practices can vary
futureScope: Useful for statistics-heavy analysis and research; Python and SQL are often complementary skills.

name: Dart
usedFor: Web and desktop apps with Flutter
pros: Supports mobile, web, and desktop Flutter targets
cons: Most useful within the Flutter ecosystem
Native platform integrations still require platform knowledge
futureScope: A practical route into cross-platform app development when paired with Flutter and platform fundamentals.

name: Ruby
cons: Fewer roles than JavaScript, Java, or Python in many regions
Runtime performance needs consideration at scale
futureScope: A productive language for existing Rails products and teams that value rapid web development.
